page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.medium is a general-purpose, entry-tier instance type powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 architecture. The instance provides 1 dedicated physical core running 1 vCPU at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, utilizing the Neoverse-V3 CPU model. The processor configuration features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. It comes equipped with 4.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory general-purpose ratio, and features baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Unlike diskless general-purpose instances, this model bundles 59 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread execution efficiency paired with the throughput constraints expected of a single vCPU. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs in the top tier at 17.04 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression demonstrates strong throughput at 36.23 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth settles at 42.93 GB/sec, and small-model LLM text generation delivers 83.87 tokens per second. Conversely, aggregate multi-core tests, such as stress-ng multi-core (1993.9) and PassMark CPU (1417.65), land in lower percentiles due strictly to the single-core constraint. In-memory operations show 3.31 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 4.1 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the m9gd.medium delivers a compact, cost-efficient deployment profile for microservices that benefit from high single-threaded efficiency and low-latency NVMe scratch space without paying for unneeded multi-core overhead. The primary tradeoff lies in concurrency; with only 1 vCPU, heavy multitasking or parallel query processing will saturate the core. The instance is suited for lightweight caching nodes, staging environments, single-worker background tasks, lightweight web endpoints, and edge data processing pipelines requiring fast local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.medium is an arm64 general-purpose instance featuring 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) based on the ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V3 architecture clocked at 3.3 GHz. Paired with 4.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio alongside a bundled 59 GB local NVMe SSD and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system excels in single-threaded data manipulation, reaching 17.04 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression and 36.23 GB/sec in gzip compression. Because it operates on a single core, aggregate compute metrics like multi-core stress-ng reflect lower overall throughput. With no GPU hardware, the m9gd.medium represents an efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated low-latency ARM compute coupled with high-speed local disk storage, such as lightweight microservices, single-threaded processing daemons, caching servers, and compact web workloads.
